Population increased in Leeds

The estimated population of Leeds in 2024 was 845,189 usual residents, a rise of 1.4% since 2023.

This meant that Leeds' rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Leeds increased by 4.4%.

Over this slightly longer period, Leeds was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Leeds

The average (median) age fell to 36.1 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Leeds has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Leeds is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Leeds' population of 845,189 usual residents was made up of:

  • 157,114 people aged 0 to 15 years, (18.6%)
  • 556,230 people aged 16 to 64 years, (65.8%)
  • 131,845 people aged 65 years and over, (15.6%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Leeds has a slightly lower proportion of people aged 65 years and over (15.6% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Leeds, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Leeds
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Leeds, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 1,622 people (0.2%). In total, there were 8,468 births and 6,846 deaths in Leeds.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 4,607 (-0.6%). There were 50,077 people entering the area and 54,684 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Leeds' population of 14,680 (1.8%) as a result of 24,985 people entering the area and 10,305 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Leeds was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Leeds in mid-2023 is 833,516.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 4,189 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 86 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 4,103 people.
